Smt. Lalita vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:10413
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Kumar Singh
 &
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ajay Kumar Nirankari
 On The 5 th Of February, 2026
 Criminal Appeal No. 801 of 2014
 Smt. Lalita
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Pramod Kumar Thakre - Advocate for the appellant.
 Ms. Swati Aseem George - Public Prosecutor for the resp
 Order

Per: Justice Vivek Kumar Singh This appeal under Section 372 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (for short "Cr.P.C) is filed by the complainant/respondent no.2 being aggrieved of judgment dated 13.01.2014 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Betul, District Betul (M.P.) in Sessions Trial No.130/2013, whereby the complainant/respondent no.2 was acquitted from the charges under Sections 376(1) and 506 Part-II of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C").
2.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Betul, District Betul (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The prosecution case in short is that on 14-04-2014 at about 08.00 PM, respondent no. 2 has committed rape upon appellant by giving threatening to kill her.

On the basis of information, police registered the offence punishable under Sections 376(1) and 506 Part -II of IPC against respondent no. 2 and after investigation, charge sheet has been filed before learned JMFC who committed the case for trial to the Court of Session.

Learned trial court after taking evidence into NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10413 2 CRA-801-2014 consideration and going through the record came to the conclusion that respondent no. 2 is not guilty and acquitted him from the charges.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the court below has committed an error in acquitting the respondent no.2.

He further submits that the court below ought to have considered the evidence of appellant (PW-1) which is supported by other prosecution witnesses, who have specifically stated in their statements against the respondent no.2.
The court below has not appreciated the evidence on record.
Learned court below has erred in believing the defence witnesses, as they were the interested witnesses and discarded the evidence of prosecution witnesses.

Hence, finding of the court below is liable to be reversed and respondent no. 2 be Smt. Lalita vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81726052/
1 convicted.
4.

entities.text: Smt. Lalita vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant at length and perused the record.

5. Considering the entire evidence on record and in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that after proper appreciation of the entire evidence on record, the court below has rightly acquitted respondent no. 2 from the charges of offences levelled against him.
We are not inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment dated 13.01.2014.
6. Accordingly, the appeal lacks merit and is hereby dismissed.

(AJAY KUM  JUDGE J  SSL Smt. Lalita vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81726052/
